mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the CPIAUCSL inflation index is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to market anticipation of future rate hikes.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly change > 0.3% over the prior 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during inflation upswings (p > 0.05), or CPIAUCSL decelerates after the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: When PAYEMS rises above its 12-month moving average, labor market strength is interpreted as supportive of corporate earnings, driving positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: No significant positive return in 60 days after trigger, or earnings revisions decline sharply in the following quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in GDPC1 (goods orders) followed within 2 months by a decline in RSAFS (retail sales) indicates shifting demand composition, predicting a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive or near-zero during such divergence events, or the pattern recurs without negative returns.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production) below its 6-month average suggests supply-side weakness, leading to a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: INDPRO recovers quickly or 5-day returns are not significantly negative during contraction phases (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 4% for three consecutive months, markets anticipate accommodative policy, resulting in a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: No significant positive return over 60 days, or FEDFUNDS rises before 60 days have elapsed.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained drop in UNRATE (unemployment) below 4% signals tight labor markets, which typically precedes equity risk-on flows and a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: No positive 20-day return during UNRATE < 4.0 periods, or unemployment rises before returns materialize.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising HOUST (household spending) without a corresponding rise in RSAFS (retail sales) suggests demand that is not supply-driven, predicting a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > HOUST_1month_lag and RSAFS <= RSAFS_1month_lag for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day returns are not negative or the pattern fails to repeat with negative returns.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in GDPC1 (goods orders) coinciding with a sharp rise in CPIAUCSL (inflation) indicates supply disruption and cost-push risk, leading to a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive or no significant effect is detected during such episodes (p > 0.05).
